name: No sudden change before the choke
explanation: No sudden P-MON-CKP change in the last 30 minutes.

name: Sudden drop of subsea pressure
explanation: P-TPT dropped suddenly within the last 30 minutes (fast event).

name: Sudden rise of subsea pressure
explanation: P-TPT rose suddenly within the last 30 minutes (fast event).

name: No sudden change of subsea pressure
explanation: No sudden P-TPT change in the last 30 minutes (slow event or none).

name: Production choke closing
explanation: The recorded opening of the production choke decreased.

name: Production choke opening unchanged
explanation: The recorded opening of the production choke has not changed.

name: Gas lift in operation
explanation: Gas-lift flow is above zero.

name: Well deliberately closed
explanation: Petrobras state label says the well is deliberately closed, so stopped flow is expected.

name: Well being restarted
explanation: The well is being restarted — cold fluid and changing pressures are expected (and hydrates are more likely).

name: Well intervention in progress
explanation: An operation is changing pressures on purpose.

name: Too few trustworthy sensors to diagnose
explanation: Fewer than 2 of the 8 key process sensors give trustworthy readings right now. Instead of guessing 'normal', the system reports that it cannot decide (incomplete information).

name: Downhole gauge frozen while subsea pressure changes
explanation: P-PDG has reported exactly the same value for over an hour while the reliable TPT sensor shows a real change. The two disagree; the thesis notes PDGs commonly freeze or fail, while TPT is considered reliable, so PDG is discounted (trust 0.2).

name: Downhole gauge sending invalid values
explanation: P-PDG is sending error codes or impossible values; diagnosis must rely on TPT and choke sensors.

name: Subsea transducer frozen
explanation: P-TPT has reported exactly the same value for over an hour.

name: Flow stopping: subsea fluid cooling
explanation: When production stops, the fluid at the subsea tree cools toward sea temperature (the thesis notes T-TPT decay indicates production stopped).

name: Flow stopping: choke outlet cooling
explanation: Less hot fluid passes the choke, so the temperature after it falls.

name: Fluid temperatures rising (TPT)
explanation: Warmer fluid at the subsea tree.

name: Fluid temperatures rising (after choke)
explanation: Warmer fluid after the production choke.

name: Hydrate-favourable conditions
explanation: Hydrates need high pressure and low temperature: pressure at the tree is up while temperature is down.

name: Flow is oscillating (TPT_CYCLE large swings)
explanation: Large repeated swings mean the flow itself is oscillating. While it oscillates, momentary ups and downs of pressure say nothing about WHERE a blockage is, so the location rules are switched off.

name: Flow is oscillating (CKP_CYCLE large swings)
explanation: Large repeated swings mean the flow itself is oscillating. While it oscillates, momentary ups and downs of pressure say nothing about WHERE a blockage is, so the location rules are switched off.

name: Flow is oscillating (TPT_T_CYCLE large swings)
explanation: Large repeated swings mean the flow itself is oscillating. While it oscillates, momentary ups and downs of pressure say nothing about WHERE a blockage is, so the location rules are switched off.

name: Restriction between downhole gauge and subsea tree
explanation: Pressure rises below and falls above the DHSV: something is blocking flow between the PDG and the TPT — where the DHSV sits.

name: Restriction near DHSV (downhole gauge unavailable)
explanation: Works without the PDG: pressure dropped suddenly at the tree and before the choke, so the blockage is below the tree.

name: Restriction near DHSV (only subsea tree sensors available)
explanation: Works with the subsea tree alone: pressure fell suddenly and the fluid is cooling (flow stopping), so something closed below the tree.

name: Restriction between subsea tree and production choke
explanation: Pressure rises at the subsea tree but falls before the choke: the blockage is in the production line between them.

name: Restriction above the subsea tree (choke pressure unavailable)
explanation: Pressure rises both downhole and at the tree, with no rise before the choke: the blockage is downstream of the tree.

name: Restriction at the production choke
explanation: Pressure rises everywhere upstream of the choke: the blockage is at the choke itself.

name: Restriction at the choke (pressure up, outlet cooling)
explanation: Pressure builds before the choke while less fluid passes it (outlet cools).

name: Restriction in the gas-lift/service line
explanation: Gas-lift pressure rises after the gas-lift choke while the gas-lift flow falls: the service line is blocked.

name: Restriction in service line (annulus side)
explanation: Pressure rises before the blockage (gas-lift side) and falls after it (annulus).

name: Spurious DHSV closure (restriction at DHSV + flow stopping)
explanation: A blockage at the DHSV with production stopping is the signature of a spurious DHSV closure.

name: Spurious DHSV closure (restriction at DHSV)
explanation: The pressure pattern places the blockage at the DHSV.

name: Against DHSV closure: temperatures rising
explanation: A closed DHSV stops flow, which cools the fluid — rising temperatures argue against it.

name: Abrupt BSW increase (surface pressure down, temperatures up)
explanation: Thesis rule: with more water, pressures near the surface fall and temperatures rise (water carries more heat).

name: Abrupt BSW increase (deep pressure up, surface down, temperatures up)
explanation: Thesis rule: deeper pressures rise, near-surface pressures fall, temperatures rise.

name: Abrupt BSW increase (gradual surface pressure decline, flow continues)
explanation: Surface pressures drift down while fluid keeps flowing and the annulus is unaffected — heavier (wetter) fluid column.

name: Against BSW: flow stopping
explanation: A BSW increase changes the fluid but does not stop the flow.

name: Severe slugging (large swings along the circuit)
explanation: Large, repeated swings at both the subsea tree and the choke: severe slugging is detectable along the whole production circuit.

name: Severe slugging (large swings at subsea tree)
explanation: The 3W paper shows slugging as swings above 10 bar at the TPT.

name: Severe slugging (large swings before choke and in temperature)
explanation: Large repeated swings in choke pressure and subsea temperature together.

name: Severe slugging (large swings in annulus and gas lift)
explanation: The slug cycle also shows in the annulus and gas-lift pressures.

name: Flow instability (small swings at subsea tree)
explanation: Tolerable, non-periodic swings in the subsea pressure.

name: Flow instability (small swings at tree and choke)
explanation: Small swings in two places along the flow path.

name: Flow instability (small swings before choke)
explanation: Small swings before the choke only — weak evidence (normal wells sometimes show this).

name: Against instability: swings are large (that is slugging)
explanation: Large repeated swings mean severe slugging rather than tolerable instability.

name: Rapid productivity loss (annulus and subsea pressures fall)
explanation: The whole system loses pressure (energy) without a blockage: the reservoir can no longer push fluid up.

name: Rapid productivity loss (pressures and temperature falling, no blockage)
explanation: Pressures and temperature decline gradually along the circuit, with no sudden drop and no blockage pattern.

name: Against productivity loss: sudden drop
explanation: Productivity loss develops over hours; a sudden drop points to a valve closure.

name: Quick restriction in PCK (choke closing + pressure up before choke)
explanation: The choke is closing and pressure builds up before it.

name: Quick restriction in PCK (sudden rise before the choke)
explanation: A blockage at the choke that appeared suddenly.

name: Quick restriction in PCK (subsea pressure up, no blockage elsewhere)
explanation: 3W paper: a PCK restriction raises pressure at TPT, PDG and before the choke; flow continues.

name: Scaling in PCK (restriction at choke, choke not moved)
explanation: Flow is restricted at the choke although nobody moved it — deposits are narrowing it.

name: Scaling in PCK (pressure before choke up, outlet cooler, no sudden change)
explanation: A slow build-up of pressure before the choke while less fluid passes it.

name: Scaling in PCK (slow restriction at choke)
explanation: Experts confirm scaling over ~72 h windows: it develops slowly, without sudden jumps.

name: Scaling in PCK (pressure before choke above normal)
explanation: Pressure before the choke has settled above this well's normal level.

name: Scaling in PCK (slow pressure build-up before the choke)
explanation: Pressure before the choke creeps up over hours with no sudden change and no operator action on the choke: deposits are slowly narrowing it (experts confirm scaling over ~72 h windows).

name: Scaling in PCK (slow build-up before choke, outlet cooling slowly)
explanation: Slowly rising pressure before the choke together with a slowly cooling outlet: less and less fluid passes the choke.

name: Against scaling: sudden rise
explanation: Scaling builds up over hours to days, not suddenly.

name: Hydrate in production line (restriction in line + flow stopping)
explanation: A blockage between the tree and the choke while production stops (T-TPT falling).

name: Hydrate in production line (restriction in line)
explanation: 3W paper: hydrate raises pressure upstream (PDG, TPT) and lowers it downstream (MON-CKP).

name: Hydrate in production line (hydrate conditions + restriction)
explanation: High pressure and low temperature at the tree favour hydrate formation.

name: Hydrate in production line (deep pressure up, tree cooling)
explanation: Pressure builds downhole while the tree cools and its pressure does not fall — blockage above the tree.

name: Hydrate in service line (restriction in service line)
explanation: The gas-lift/service line is blocked.

name: Hydrate in service line (gas-lift pressure up)
explanation: Gas-lift pressure after the choke rises while injecting — the line downstream is harder to push through.

name: Hydrate in service line (gas-lift flow down while injecting)
explanation: Gas-lift flow falls without a drop in injection pressure.

name: Operation in progress explains the pattern (Spurious closure of DHSV)
explanation: Operators are shutting in, restarting or intervening on the well, so pressure and flow changes are expected consequences of the operation, not evidence of this fault.

name: Operation in progress explains the pattern (Rapid productivity loss)
explanation: Operators are shutting in, restarting or intervening on the well, so pressure and flow changes are expected consequences of the operation, not evidence of this fault.

explanation: Operators are shutting in, restarting or intervening on the well, so pressure and flow changes are expected consequences of the operation, not evidence of this fault.

explanation: Operators are shutting in, restarting or intervening on the well, so pressure and flow changes are expected consequences of the operation, not evidence of this fault.

explanation: Operators are shutting in, restarting or intervening on the well, so pressure and flow changes are expected consequences of the operation, not evidence of this fault.

name: Operation in progress explains the pattern (Severe slugging)
explanation: Operators are shutting in, restarting or intervening on the well, so pressure and flow changes are expected consequences of the operation, not evidence of this fault.

name: Operation in progress explains the pattern (Flow instability)
explanation: Operators are shutting in, restarting or intervening on the well, so pressure and flow changes are expected consequences of the operation, not evidence of this fault.

name: Operation in progress explains the pattern (Hydrate in service line)
explanation: Operators are shutting in, restarting or intervening on the well, so pressure and flow changes are expected consequences of the operation, not evidence of this fault.

name: Hydrate remediation operation in progress
explanation: Depressurization, flushing and bullheading are the standard ways to clear a hydrate plug; such an operation suggests a hydrate is being dealt with. (Context rule — its effect is reported separately in the evaluation.)

name: Restart raises hydrate likelihood
explanation: Cold restarts are a classic time for hydrate formation.

name: Answer NO to Q_DHSV_COMMANDED
explanation: Nobody commanded the closure, so it was spurious.

name: Answer YES to Q_DHSV_COMMANDED
explanation: The closure was commanded on purpose — expected, not a fault.

name: Answer YES to Q_DHSV_HYDRAULICS
explanation: Spurious closures usually happen with no surface indication (normal control-line pressure).

name: Answer YES to Q_WATER_SAMPLE
explanation: A sample directly confirms the higher water cut.

name: Answer NO to Q_WATER_SAMPLE
explanation: The sample shows no water-cut increase.

name: Answer YES to Q_SEPARATOR_SURGES
explanation: Regular surges at the separator are the classic sign of slugging.

name: Answer NO to Q_SEPARATOR_SURGES
explanation: No regular surges: the swings are not periodic.

name: Answer NO to Q_SEPARATOR_SURGES
explanation: Disturbances without a regular cycle point to instability.

name: Answer YES to Q_SETPOINT_CHANGE
explanation: A recent set-point change can trigger instability.

name: Answer YES to Q_SETPOINT_CHANGE
explanation: The choke was moved deliberately — an operator action, not an unwanted restriction.

name: Answer YES to Q_WELL_TEST
explanation: The well test confirms the well is producing less than expected.

name: Answer YES to Q_CHOKE_LOCAL
explanation: The choke is physically more closed than intended.

name: Answer NO to Q_CHOKE_LOCAL
explanation: The choke position is correct, so the restriction is inside it (deposits).

name: Answer NO to Q_CHOKE_LOCAL
explanation: The choke position is correct.

name: Answer YES to Q_SCALE_HISTORY
explanation: Scaling tends to recur where water chemistry favours it.

name: Answer YES to Q_HYDRATE_CURVE
explanation: Conditions are inside the hydrate-formation region.

name: Answer NO to Q_HYDRATE_CURVE
explanation: Hydrates cannot form outside their pressure–temperature region.

name: Answer YES to Q_HYDRATE_CURVE
explanation: Conditions are inside the hydrate-formation region.

name: Answer YES to Q_RECENT_RESTART
explanation: Shut-ins and cold restarts are a common time for hydrates to form.

name: Answer YES to Q_RECENT_RESTART
explanation: Shut-ins and cold restarts are a common time for hydrates to form.

name: Answer YES to Q_SERVICE_LINE_INHIBITOR
explanation: Without inhibitor, water left in the line can turn into hydrate.
